author: emily_dickinson

I will tell you what is in my mind,
 If only for this time;
 The rest I cannot tell--the rest it dies,
 For evermore is mine!
 My very being in life or death
 Is yours forever more;
 Oh, but think that it may be your fate,
 That so soon it must go!

A small frog came hopping up to me, asking for some things.
"Can you tell me how to make a cake?" said the little creature.
I replied, "It's very easy; just follow these four features."
First, mix your ingredients together until they are all mixed.

The first time I went inside this
Old man-house was when I was six years old;
I had never been into it before, so much
Was the house known for its haunted past;
All around me were skeletons of furniture —
Some smashed, some torn asunder by fire,

author: john_masefield
text:
The men were all as one, And the women said amen;
They drew a long bow o'er the hills, They drew a mighty strain,
And it cracked and split upon its string, The silver moon was in the sky;
Then there came up from the east A cloud that looked like an eye.

I know not why, but I think they feared It would be an evil sign:
For ever since old Adam wore His first apple on his chin,
Man has been afraid to look Up into the face of God.

text: "My Mother Told Me What To Do," written by William Butler Yeats, is an example of Irish-style poetry. It follows traditional themes found in Irish literature, such as love, family, and the struggle for independence. The language used in this excerpt showcases the use of Gaelic words and phrases that are characteristic of Irish poetry. Additionally, the repetition of "my" at the beginning of each line emphasizes personal connection and ownership over one's actions.

text:
I came to my knees,

My heart’s blood on these stairs;
A drop from every vein
Fell to the floor like rain—
So I could never again
Be alone for one more hour
Without this dread fear rising up
And then bursting out into
The words that all men have said
But only God can answer:
‘Where is your brother?’

(I used "The Black Sheep" from On the Road by Jack Kerouac) The black sheep was born with no ears and he said, “What’s that on my nose?” The barber came to shave him but there were not enough scissors in his pocket. Like whispers from afar.

It calls to him softly:
"Who are you?" it asks.
The man turns around and sees—
His shadow!

In this article, the author describes an experiment conducted by scientists from Harvard University that aimed to develop and test a new method for detecting and identifying viruses using computer algorithms. The researchers collected samples of nasal fluid from individuals who had been infected with various types of influenza A viruses (H1N1) and tested them using their algorithm. They were able to identify all 85% of viral RNA fragments found in the sample as belonging to the H1N2 virus type. This technique could potentially help us better understand how these viruses spread through populations and could be used in future disease outbreak investigations or surveillance
